messages.subject: incomplete seqz file generated
parts:

messages.author: dad6980b76d10753
messages.subject: Re: incomplete seqz file generated
parts:
Hi Igor,

Thanks for using Sequenza!
You should check the GC file, and the fasta file you used to generate it: the order of the chromosome should be similar in all 3 files.
I bet this is the problem: some reference are ordered by chromosome size, so chrX is right after chr7.
The script skipped all the other chromosomes to reach chrX, and after processing it there was nothing left to process in the pileup (well there should be chrY...).
To verify this you could look at the output of something like: 

zcat hg19_gc50.txt.gz | grep variableStep | uniq

I'm sorry about that, I kept the script really simple so it can't figure out shuffled-chromosomes files.
A universal solution for this problem is to process the bam/pileups chromosome by chromosome, and then merge or perform other operations on the files afterwards. It's also considerably faster (~1h per exome).

There is an example in the wiki on how to use the "wrapper":
https://bitbucket.org/ffavero/sequenza/wiki/Sequenza_Utils#markdown-header-wrapper-to-parallelize-standardize-execution

Best

Francesco
